Fix one()/only() dropping a falsy user-supplied exception

`one(it, too_long=exc)` and `only(it, too_long=exc)` used
`raise too_long or ValueError(msg)`, so a `too_long`/`too_short` whose
instances are falsy (e.g. an Exception subclass overriding `__bool__`)
was discarded and the default `ValueError` raised instead.

Switch to explicit `is not None` checks, and only build the default
message when no custom exception is supplied so a faulty `__repr__` on
the iterable's items can't shadow the requested exception.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Skip the transliteration backend for ASCII text (#201)

Every backend (text-unidecode, Unidecode, anyascii) maps 7-bit ASCII to
itself, so ASCII input no longer imports one. With text-unidecode this
avoids loading its ~3 MB table for the common case of ASCII slugs.
Output is unchanged, including the frozen legacy differential.
